Lesson 5 of 5

Payments and ledger-style systems

Money movement demands idempotency, auditability, reconciliation, and a conservative approach to asynchronous side effects.

25-35 min HLD flow Common product design patterns 4 guided stops

Why this lesson matters

Even if you never design a payments product in production, this lesson forces precise thinking about correctness under failure.

Interview framing

Even if you never design a payments product in production, this lesson forces precise thinking about correctness under failure.

What to say first

  • Use immutable ledger events or equivalent audit records.

    Show likely answer
    • Use immutable ledger events or equivalent audit records.
    • Represent money movement as balanced ledger entries or state transitions so you can audit and reconcile every step.
    • The core ledger path often requires strong correctness, while email, analytics, and some partner updates can be asynchronous.

  • Make transaction creation idempotent.

    Show likely answer
    • Make transaction creation idempotent.
    • Persist the canonical transaction result before side effects
    • Letting downstream notifications define transaction truth.

Operational safeguards

Retries, duplicate callbacks, partial outages, and compliance audits are normal, so design the workflow as a recoverable state machine.

Call these points out explicitly

  • Hold suspicious transactions for review when needed

Common pitfalls

What to avoid

  • Using write-behind caches for balances.
  • Letting downstream notifications define transaction truth.
  • Ignoring external callback duplication and delayed settlement.
